title: Rav Chinena bar Kahana
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rav’s student, as in [Rosh Hashanah 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.19b.5) and [Beitzah 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.6a.2), where Rav Chinena bar Kahana says in Rav’s name: “From the days of Ezra onward we have not found Elul intercalated.” In [Beitzah 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.22b.2) and [Rosh Hashanah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.32a.15) the formula omits “in Rav’s name.” In [Avodah Zarah 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.20b.8) he said: “In the school of Rav they say: One who wants his dead not to decay should turn him on his face.”

We likewise find Rav Chinena bar Kahana speaking in Shmuel’s name, as in [Ketubot 65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.65a.4) and [72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.72a.12) and Hyman’s Bava Kamma 113b (compare [Bava Kamma 113a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.113a.15), which names Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana), and again in [Taanit 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.30a.13). Hyman also reads Rav Chinena bar Kahana transmitting in Rav Assi’s name at Eruvin 55a. He regards “Rav Ashi” as a printing error and reports Rav Assi in the Venice edition. In [Shabbat 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.96a.2) he spoke in Rabbi Elazar’s name (Hyman proposes Elazar, not Rabbi Eliezer, following Dikdukei Soferim).[^3] He is mentioned in [Sanhedrin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.9): “Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana said: Salted meat, so long as it is like shelamim,” etc.[^4]

notes.text: The Assi/Ashi and Elazar/Eliezer choices are Hyman’s stated textual corrections, not blanket normalization. The Sanhedrin salted-meat statement is abridged as supplied.

Rosh Hashanah 19b directly names Rabbi Chinena bar Kahana reporting Rav; the Rav/Rabbi forms remain as supplied in each source. The bounded Eruvin 55a comparison did not locate the cited Assi transmission. Hyman’s Venice and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain attributed to him; those exact editions were not independently inspected.

[Shabbat 96a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.96a.2) reads Rabbi Eliezer. [Taanit 30a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.30a.13) gives the salted-meat rule in Shmuel’s name, while [Sanhedrin 70a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.9) gives it directly in Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana’s name.

The consulted Bava Kamma has Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana transmit Shmuel’s explanation about an unrestricted customs collector. The same chain recurs at [Bava Kamma 113a:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.113a.18) and [Bava Kamma 113a:20](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.113a.20). Hyman supplies 113b and uses the title Rav in his parenthesis.
